organization: Department of Financial Services (Ministry of Finance); SIDBI (nodal agency)
schemeType: Composite Term Loan + Working Capital (Bank loan scheme)
description: Facilitates composite bank loans between Rs.10 lakh and Rs.1 crore to at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower per bank branch, for setting up a new greenfield enterprise in manufacturing, services, or trading.
entrepreneurshipRelevance: Core entrepreneurship scheme; directly funds setting up a new business for SC/ST/women entrepreneurs.
genderRequirement: At least one woman borrower per bank branch (any category); SC/ST borrowers may be any gender
otherBeneficiaryConditions: Borrower/promoter must hold at least 51% controlling stake; must be a first-time entrepreneur for a greenfield project
beneficiaryContribution: Minimum 10% of project cost as margin money (up to 15% via convergence with other schemes)
interestRate: Bank's lowest applicable rate for the category (base rate + tenor premium + up to 3%); not centrally fixed, varies by bank
eligibleActivities: Any new (greenfield) enterprise in manufacturing, services, or trading sector
eligibilityRules: Applicant must be SC and/or ST and/or woman entrepreneur; age 18+; project must be greenfield; applicant must hold >=51% controlling stake
mandatoryConditions: First-time entrepreneur; greenfield (new) project only; not a defaulter to any bank/financial institution
applicationMethod: Online via Stand-Up Mitra portal, then processed by the nominated bank branch
applicationAuthority: Scheduled Commercial Bank branches, coordinated by SIDBI/Department of Financial Services
channelisingAgency: Public and private sector Scheduled Commercial Banks; SIDBI (nodal)
sourceDocument: Department of Financial Services - Stand-Up India Scheme guidelines
verificationNotes: Core loan range (Rs.10L-Rs.1Cr), 7-year repayment and 18-month moratorium cross-confirmed across NSFDC's official page and multiple secondary sources. Several 2025-2026 news reports describe a proposed revamp that would double the ceiling to Rs.2 crore, but this was NOT confirmed as officially implemented as of verification date. RE-CHECK standupmitra.in / dfs.gov.in before final demo if the exact ceiling matters.
dataStatus: verified (re-check loan ceiling closer to demo date)
maximumProjectCostRaw: Loan is composite (term loan + working capital); typically covers 85% of project cost

organization: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; implemented by KVIC, State KVIBs, and District Industries Centres (DICs)
description: Credit-linked subsidy scheme for setting up new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector. The bank finances the project as a loan; the government subsidises 15-35% of the project cost as margin money, held in a 3-year term deposit.
entrepreneurshipRelevance: Directly funds new micro-enterprise setup with a government subsidy on the loan.
genderRequirement: None mandatory; women fall under the Special Category with a higher subsidy rate
otherBeneficiaryConditions: Only one person per family eligible; minimum 8th-standard pass required if project cost exceeds Rs.10 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs.5 lakh (service)
interestRate: Normal bank MSE lending rate, typically ~11-12% p.a. (varies by bank)
repaymentPeriod: Bank term-loan tenor per sanction, typically up to 3 years post subsidy adjustment (subject to bank terms)
businessTypes: Trading/Business (trading capped at max 10% of a state's annual financial allocation)
supportedPurposes: working capital (as part of composite loan)
eligibleActivities: Wide range of non-farm micro-enterprise activities per the KVIC-approved activity list
eligibilityRules: Age 18+; new project only; one beneficiary per family; minimum 8th pass for larger projects
mandatoryConditions: Must complete Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training before margin money is released
exclusionConditions: Existing PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA beneficiaries not eligible for a fresh first loan under this scheme; project cost exceeding the sector cap
optionalDocuments: EDP completion certificate (post-sanction, required before margin money release)
applicationAuthority: KVIC / State KVIBs / District Industries Centres (implementing agencies); Banks (financing)
channelisingAgency: Public Sector Banks, RRBs, Cooperative Banks, and private banks empanelled with KVIC
sourceDocument: PMEGP Guidelines (KVIC, certified 2022 revision; project-cost ceiling updated per Union Budget 2023-24)
sourceDate: 2022 (guideline revision); manufacturing ceiling raised to Rs.50L effective post Budget 2023-24
verificationNotes: Subsidy grid (General: 15% urban/25% rural; Special: 25% urban/35% rural) and project cost ceilings (Rs.50L manufacturing / Rs.20L service) cross-verified against KVIC's own certified guidelines PDF and multiple independent secondary sources; figures are consistent.
maximumLoanAmountRaw: Bank credit of 90-95% of project cost (up to ~Rs.47.5 lakh manufacturing / ~Rs.19 lakh service, after margin money)

schemeName: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY / MUDRA loans)
organization: MUDRA Ltd. (Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency), Ministry of Finance
schemeType: Collateral-free micro loan (refinance scheme operated via banks/NBFCs/MFIs)
description: Collateral-free loans up to Rs.20 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm micro and small enterprises, structured across four tiers: Shishu, Kishor, Tarun, and Tarun Plus.
entrepreneurshipRelevance: Directly funds micro-enterprise setup and expansion at multiple scales, from very small to established micro businesses.
targetGroups: no caste/gender restriction, though women/SC/ST/minority applicants are often prioritised by lending banks
otherBeneficiaryConditions: Business must be non-corporate and non-farm; Tarun Plus requires a prior successfully repaid Tarun-category loan
beneficiaryContribution: Varies by lender; not centrally fixed
interestRate: Lender's MCLR + spread; not fixed centrally by government, varies by bank/NBFC
repaymentPeriod: Typically up to 5 years (varies by lender and tier)
businessTypes: Allied non-farm agricultural activities (e.g. dairy, poultry, beekeeping)
eligibleActivities: Tailoring, kirana/trading, food processing, repair services, transport vehicles, salons, small manufacturing, allied activities
eligibilityRules: Indian resident; age 18+; non-corporate non-farm income-generating activity; no major default on existing loans
mandatoryConditions: Aadhaar, PAN, and bank account mandatory; business proof (GST/Udyam/Shop Act licence/partnership deed) required for Kishor/Tarun/Tarun Plus
exclusionConditions: Pure crop-agriculture activities not covered (Kisan Credit Card applies instead); corporate entities not eligible
applicationMethod: Apply at any PSU/private bank, RRB, Small Finance Bank, or NBFC branch; or online via Udyamimitra/Jan Samarth portal
applicationAuthority: Scheduled Commercial Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, NBFCs, MFIs (Member Lending Institutions)
channelisingAgency: Member Lending Institutions (MLIs), refinanced by MUDRA Ltd.
sourceDocument: PIB Press Release: enhancement of Mudra loan limit to Rs.20 lakh (Tarun Plus)
verificationNotes: Rs.20 lakh Tarun Plus ceiling and the four-tier structure confirmed via official PIB press release. Interest rates are lender-specific and NOT fixed by government -- do not hardcode a single percentage in the eligibility engine.
maximumProjectCostRaw: Loan typically covers the full micro-project cost within tier limits

organization: National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC), Ministry of Tribal Affairs
description: Term loan for any viable income-generation project costing up to Rs.50 lakh per unit for Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs, with financial assistance up to 90% of project cost.
entrepreneurshipRelevance: Core entrepreneurship/self-employment funding for Scheduled Tribe persons.
genderRequirement: None mandatory (a separate exclusive scheme, Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana, exists for ST women)
otherBeneficiaryConditions: For SHGs/co-operative societies, a minimum of 80% of members must belong to Scheduled Tribes
beneficiaryContribution: Remaining balance (~10%) via subsidy/promoter contribution/margin money
interestRate: 6% to 10% p.a. depending on loan slab
repaymentPeriod: 5 to 10 years depending on loan amount
moratoriumPeriod: Not centrally fixed; per Channelising Agency sanction terms
businessTypes: Any viable business, trade, or service activity
supportedPurposes: Setting up a new income-generating unit
eligibilityRules: Applicant must belong to a Scheduled Tribe community; annual family income within double the poverty line (~Rs.3 lakh); not a defaulter to any bank/financial institution
mandatoryConditions: ST caste certificate; project must be assessed as viable by the Channelising Agency
exclusionConditions: Applicants above the income threshold; loan defaulters
applicationMethod: Apply through the State Channelising Agency (SCA) in the prescribed format
channelisingAgency: State ST Finance/Development Corporations; nominated banks; NEDFi (for NE states)
sourceDocument: NSTFDC Scheme Guidelines; PIB press release (Lok Sabha reply, Ministry of Tribal Affairs)
verificationNotes: Income limit of Rs.3,00,000 p.a. (rural and urban) directly confirmed on the official NSTFDC Term Loan eligibility page (nstfdc.tribal.gov.in, frm_term_loan.aspx) on 2026-08-29. Note: the source states this figure is revised from time to time based on Planning Commission poverty-line norms, so it should be periodically re-checked in future use, but is treated as current and verified for this hackathon.

organization: National Backward Classes Finance & Development Corporation (NBCFDC), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
description: Loans for income-generating activities for members of Backward Classes with annual family income up to Rs.5 lakh, up to Rs.25 lakh per beneficiary.
entrepreneurshipRelevance: Core self-employment/entrepreneurship funding for OBC individuals.
targetGroups: OBC (Other Backward Classes, as notified by Central/State Government)
genderRequirement: None mandatory (a separate exclusive scheme, New Swarnima, exists for OBC women)
otherBeneficiaryConditions: OBC caste certificate from the Central list (ncbc.gov.in) or the applicable State list is required
interestRate: Varies by loan slab; concessional rates for smaller loan amounts per NBCFDC's published rate structure
repaymentPeriod: Up to 8 years, including moratorium (per NBCFDC General Loan structure)
eligibleActivities: Wide range of viable income-generating activities across the listed sectors
eligibilityRules: Applicant must belong to a notified OBC caste; annual family income up to Rs.5 lakh
mandatoryConditions: OBC caste certificate from competent authority
exclusionConditions: Annual family income above Rs.5 lakh; non-OBC applicants
applicationMethod: Apply through the State Channelising Agency (SCA) or Channel Partner
applicationAuthority: NBCFDC (apex), via State Channelising Agencies/Channel Partners
channelisingAgency: State-level OBC finance/development corporations; nominated banks/NBFCs
sourceDocument: NBCFDC Individual Loan Scheme page (official website)
sourceDate: Current as published on official site (undated revision -- recommend periodic re-check)
verificationNotes: Core figures (Rs.5 lakh income limit, Rs.25 lakh max loan, 85:15 financing pattern) taken directly from NBCFDC's own official website page for the Individual Loan Scheme -- considered the highest-confidence source used in this dataset.
maximumProjectCostRaw: Loan covers 85% of project cost (implied project cost up to approximately Rs.29.4 lakh)

schemeName: NHFDC Self-Employment Loan Scheme (Persons with Disabilities)
organization: National Handicapped Finance and Development Corporation (NHFDC), Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
description: Concessional loans to persons with disabilities (40%+ disability) for setting up self-employment ventures across business, trading, transport, small industry, and agriculture-allied activities.
entrepreneurshipRelevance: Core entrepreneurship/self-employment funding for persons with disabilities.
targetGroups: PwD (Persons with Disabilities, 40%+ disability as defined under the RPwD Act 2016)
genderRequirement: None mandatory; women with disabilities receive an additional 1% interest rebate across NHFDC schemes
otherBeneficiaryConditions: Applicant should not already be covered under another central/state government financing scheme for the same purpose
beneficiaryContribution: Varies by loan slab; not centrally fixed in sources reviewed
interestRate: Concessional, varies by loan slab and category; additional 1% rebate for women with disabilities
moratoriumPeriod: Not centrally fixed; per SCA sanction terms
eligibleActivities: Wide range of income-generating self-employment activities suited to the applicant's ability and training
eligibilityRules: Indian citizen with 40%+ disability; age 18-60 (14+ in case of intellectual disability, per one source); relevant technical/vocational qualification or experience preferred
mandatoryConditions: Disability certificate (40%+) from competent medical authority; applicant should not be a loan defaulter
exclusionConditions: Disability below 40%; already covered under another government financing scheme for the same purpose
optionalDocuments: Caste certificate (if also SC/ST/OBC, for combined-benefit consideration)
applicationMethod: Apply through the State Channelising Agency in the prescribed format; loans above Rs.10 lakh sanctioned directly by NHFDC
applicationAuthority: NHFDC (apex), via State Channelising Agencies / select nationalised banks / RRBs in select states
channelisingAgency: State Channelising Agencies (SCAs) nominated by respective state governments
sourceDocument: NHFDC scheme summary (compiled from Vikaspedia and state SCA portals citing NHFDC norms)
sourceDate: Not explicitly dated in sources reviewed
verificationNotes: Income limit directly confirmed on the official NHFDC website (nhfdc.nic.in), Offerings > Beneficiary Guidelines > Eligibility Requirements, on 2026-08-29: annual family income must not exceed Rs.5,00,000 for BOTH rural and urban areas, effective 7 January 2026 (Credit/Loan-Based Schemes). No income criterion applies to Skill Development Training Programmes. This corrects the earlier Rs.5L urban / Rs.3L rural split, which was based on secondary sources and is now known to be outdated/incorrect -- the current rule is a single flat Rs.5 lakh limit for both areas.
maximumProjectCostRaw: Varies by activity category (business/trading, transport, small industry each have separate published sub-limits)

organization: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
description: Provides loans up to 90% of project cost (project cost ceiling Rs.50 lakh; term loan up to Rs.45 lakh) to Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs for income-generating activities.
entrepreneurshipRelevance: Core entrepreneurship/self-employment funding for Scheduled Caste persons.
genderRequirement: None mandatory; women receive a 0.5% interest rebate under some NSFDC schemes (e.g. education loan)
otherBeneficiaryConditions: Applicant must not be a defaulter to any bank/financial institution
interestRate: NSFDC charges 4% p.a. to the Channelising Agency, which in turn charges 8% p.a. to the beneficiary
eligibleActivities: Wide range of income-generating activities per NSFDC's approved sector list
eligibilityRules: Applicant must belong to a Scheduled Caste community; annual family income within the prescribed limit; not a loan defaulter
mandatoryConditions: SC caste certificate; project appraisal/viability assessment by the Channelising Agency
exclusionConditions: Income above the prescribed limit; loan defaulters
applicationMethod: Apply through the State Channelising Agency (SCA) in the prescribed NSFDC format
channelisingAgency: State SC Development Corporations (SCDCs); Public Sector Banks; Regional Rural Banks
sourceDocument: NSFDC Term Loan Scheme page (official site); PIB Press Release on SC loan provisions
verificationNotes: Income limit of Rs.3,00,000 p.a. (rural and urban, effective from 08.03.2018) for Credit Based Schemes directly confirmed on the official NSFDC Eligibility Criteria page (nsfdc.nic.in/en/eligibility-criteria) on 2026-08-29. This supersedes the earlier Rs.5 lakh figure taken from a PIB release, which was likely referring to a different NSFDC scheme or programme. Loan amount, interest rate, and repayment period were separately confirmed on the official nsfdc.nic.in Term Loan page.

organization: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
description: Small-ticket loans for Scheduled Caste individuals to set up micro income-generating units costing up to Rs.1,40,000, financed up to 90% of project cost with a maximum loan of Rs.1.25 lakh.
entrepreneurshipRelevance: Directly matches the PS-cited 'Micro Finance Scheme for small projects (up to Rs.1.40 lakh)' -- the smallest-ticket entry point for first-time SC micro-entrepreneurs.
otherBeneficiaryConditions: Applicant must not be a defaulter to any bank/financial institution
interestRate: NSFDC charges 2.5% p.a. to the Channelising Agency, which in turn charges 6.5% p.a. to the beneficiary
businessTypes: Micro trade and service units (very small scale)
supportedPurposes: Setting up a very small income-generating unit
eligibleActivities: Betel leaf shop, bakery, candle making, cycle repair, goat rearing, beauty parlour, vegetable vending, incense stick making, fish vending, milch animal rearing, papad/pickle manufacturing, tea shop, and similar viable micro-activities
eligibilityRules: Applicant must belong to Scheduled Caste community; annual family income within Rs.3 lakh; project cost within Rs.1.40 lakh
mandatoryConditions: SC caste certificate; project cost must not exceed the Rs.1.40 lakh ceiling
exclusionConditions: Project cost above Rs.1.40 lakh (use Term Loan Scheme instead); income above prescribed limit; loan defaulters
applicationMethod: Apply through the State Channelising Agency (SCA) in the prescribed NSFDC format
channelisingAgency: State SC Development Corporations (SCDCs); Public Sector Banks; Regional Rural Banks
sourceDocument: NSFDC Micro Credit Finance scheme page (official site)
sourceDate: Current as published on official site
verificationNotes: Core figures (Rs.1.40 lakh project cost ceiling, Rs.1.25 lakh max loan, 2.5%/6.5% interest structure, 3-year repayment with 3-month moratorium) directly confirmed on nsfdc.nic.in/en/micro-credit-finance and cross-checked against 3 independent secondary sources citing the same page -- all consistent. Income limit (Rs.3 lakh) taken from NSFDC's general eligibility norm, consistent with the corrected NSFDC007 figure.

organization: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
description: One-time loan assistance for Scheduled Caste students pursuing full-time professional/technical courses in India or abroad, up to Rs.30 lakh (India) or Rs.40 lakh (abroad), or 90% of course fee, whichever is less.
entrepreneurshipRelevance: Matches the PS-cited 'Educational Loan Scheme' -- supports the skilling/education pathway that can precede or complement entrepreneurship for SC youth.
genderRequirement: None mandatory; women beneficiaries receive an additional 0.5% interest rebate
otherBeneficiaryConditions: No other education loan or scholarship should be availed for the same course; one-time assistance only
beneficiaryContribution: Remaining ~10% of course fee (or full excess above the cap)
interestRate: India: NSFDC charges 2% p.a. to SCA, which charges 6% p.a. to beneficiary. Abroad: NSFDC charges 3% p.a. to SCA, which charges 7% p.a. to beneficiary. Women get an additional 0.5% rebate in both cases.
repaymentPeriod: Up to 10 years (loans up to Rs.10 lakh); up to 12 years (loans above Rs.10 lakh)
moratoriumPeriod: 6 months after course completion or securing employment, whichever is earlier
businessTypes: Not applicable (educational loan, not a business loan)
supportedPurposes: Admission fee, tuition fee, books, stationery, equipment, examination fee, hostel/mess expenses, insurance premium, travel/visa expenses (for abroad study), caution money, development fund, clothing allowance
eligibleActivities: Regular full-time Professional/Technical courses at the graduate level and higher (e.g. engineering, medicine, management, architecture) recognized/approved by the Government, in India or abroad
eligibilityRules: Applicant must belong to Scheduled Caste community; annual family income within Rs.3 lakh; must have secured admission (merit-based) to a recognized full-time professional/technical course; no other loan/scholarship for the same course
mandatoryConditions: SC caste certificate; proof of admission; income certificate
exclusionConditions: Part-time or non-professional/non-technical courses; applicants already receiving another loan/scholarship for the same course; income above prescribed limit
requiredDocuments: proof of admission with fee schedule
optionalDocuments: Foreign exchange permit, institute ID card (for abroad study cases)
applicationMethod: Apply through the State Channelising Agency (SCA) in the prescribed NSFDC format
channelisingAgency: State SC Development Corporations (SCDCs); Public Sector Banks; Regional Rural Banks
sourceDocument: NSFDC Educational Loan Scheme page (official site)
sourceDate: Current as published on official site
verificationNotes: Core figures (Rs.30L India / Rs.40L abroad cap, 90% of course fee rule, 6%/7% beneficiary interest rates, 10/12-year repayment tiers, 6-month post-course moratorium) cross-confirmed across 6+ independent secondary sources, all citing the same official nsfdc.nic.in/en/educational-loan-scheme page. Income limit (Rs.3 lakh) consistent with NSFDC's general eligibility norm.
maximumProjectCostRaw: Actual course fee, capped at Rs.30 lakh (India) / Rs.40 lakh (abroad) or 90% of course fee, whichever is less
minimumAgeRaw: Not specified (student must have secured admission)
